The accessible Cao--Chen abstract describes face structure of square doubly substochastic matrices, not metric angles; its inaccessible full text is an explicit unresolved priority risk rather than supposed negative evidence. Targeted published-finding searches retrieved vertex degrees, John ellipsoids and covariance statements about the matching family, not this boundary angle classification. Existing own-ledger entries on partial-permutation Hausdorff gaps and partial permutohedron edge lengths do not imply this ridge statement. Historical uniqueness is not certified. value.rationale: A complete codimension-two Euclidean angle spectrum is a natural metric invariant of the widely studied bipartite matching/partial permutation polytope family. The all-pairs polar-neighborliness threshold \(\min(p,q)=3\) and the unique \((2,2)\) reversal from acute to obtuse average angle distinguish genuinely different boundary geometry. Exact multiplicities apply without face enumeration in arbitrary dimensions, and the square asymptotic quantifies disappearance of the mean defect. These go beyond a facet recount or a trivial normalization.
